why: The sealed assertion requires EVERY surviving annotation to extract a byte string the pre-edit record already held, with no exemption for a feature whose own bases the edit changed - it omits the touched() guard its four siblings use (test_coords_edit_shift.py:60,76; test_coords_gui_edit.py:84,105,128), and its own docstring says 'downstream' while the assertion ranges over all features. CO-14 requires features 'shifted for the edit, the way the GUI's own edit path does via shift_annotations', and that function's contract is that a feature CONTAINING the edit grows with it ('those bases are still its bases'). For CO-14's pinned edit - insert 30 A's at position 3000 of NC_001699.1 - five of the 28 features strictly contain position 3000 and the app at d22ffc8 grows each correctly: source (0,5130)->(0,5160); prim_transcript - (2526,5115)->(2526,5145); gene - (2602,5013)->(2602,5043); CDS - [(4770,5013),(2602,4426)]->[(4800,5043),(2602,4456)]; exon - (2602,4426)->(2602,4456). Each post-edit extract is that feature's own pre-edit extract with the 30 inserted bases spliced in at the corresponding offset (reverse-complemented on the four minus-strand features; inside the second part of the join for the CDS), verified against Bio.SeqFeature.extract on the pinned bytes and against pinned sha256 digests. The other 23 features extract byte-identically and the file's other 13 assertions pass. Satisfying the sealed assertion would require dropping those five - which CO-14's own wording forbids, which drops the whole-plasmid source feature (1..5130) on every insertion, the loss #96 exists to fix, and which - simulated - leaves the saved record with 23 features instead of 28 so that test_coords_gui_edit.py:92, which pairs saved.features[i] with before[i] positionally, misaligns and reports 14 wrong features starting (1, 'rep_origin', '[0:12](+)'). The app is right; the round-1 assertion does not express CO-14.
